notes.title: Mutants: Genesis - Balance Patch Season 2
notes.content:
Dear Psycogs,

Welcome to this second balance patch. You'll find Nerfs and Buffs and reworks of certain cards.

[b]This patch is already deployed![/b]


[h2][b]Objectives[/b][/h2]

Season 2 was far better balanced in terms of deck composition. However, we continue to see Zoo decks having a domineering position over the others. 

This balance patch main objective is to lessen Zoo impact so that the current meta changes, and give a push to two deck archetypes currently absent in the competitive scene : Boneyard and Tactics.


[h3][b]NERFS[/b][/h3]


[list]
[*] [i][b]Cernunnos[/b][/i]
[/list]

Cernunnos currently has too high statistics. Instead of reducing these statistics, we increase the EVO required to evolve. 

[b]Evolution curve[/b] : 

EVO necessary to evolve increases from [1-2-3-4] to [3-4-5-7].

[list]
[*] [i][b]Solar Lampyrion[/b][/i]
[/list]

The previous rework of Solar Lampyrion made it a lot stronger, but too versatile. We rebalance its overall potential by reducing its offensive power, without changing its support ability. 

[b]New statistics:[/b] ATK reduced from [8] to [6]

[b]Solar Eruption ability:[/b] Area damage reduced from [3] to [2]

[list]
[*] [i][b]Rakshasa[/b][/i]
[/list]

This mutant introduced in the Pioneer Drop is currently too powerful with the Forged Orb generation. To reduce its raw power, we slightly reduce its HP value and introduce a limitation to its Unsheathe ability.

[b]New statistics: [/b]

HP reduced from [3-5-7-8-9] to [2-4-6-7-8]

[b]Tiger Rage ability: [/b]

[i]Before[/i]

Unsheathe - Whenever this mutant is equipped with an Orb, it deals damage equal to its ATK to a random opposing mutant. 

[i]After[/i]

Unsheathe - Once per turn, when this mutant is equipped with an Orb, it deals damage equal to its ATK to a random opposing mutant. 

[list]
[*] [i][b]Genshiryoku[/b][/i]
[/list]

This mutant had a too massive impact as soon as it arrived in play, especially in Zoo archetypes able to trigger Kaiju domination during a single turn through support cards. 

[b]New statistics: [/b]

HP reduced from [3-5-7-10-13] to [2-4-6-9-12] 

ATK reduced from [3-5-7-9-11] à [2-4-6-8-10]

[b]Kaiju Domination ability: [/b]

ATK bonus reduced from [1-2-2-3-3] to [1-1-2-2-3]. 

HP bonus reduced from [1-1-2-3-3] to [1-1-2-2-3]

[list]
[*] [i][b]Leviathan[/b][/i]
[/list]

Contrary to our previous announcement in July, the damage of Leviathan’s Tsunami at Bronze rank have not changed. We realign them according to the announcement.

[b]Tsunami ability: [/b]

Area Damage to Buildings reduced from [1-2-2-2-3] to [1-1-2-2-3]

[list]
[*] [i][b]Defensive Shield[/b][/i]
[/list]

This is the most-played buiding in the game. We have decided to increase the EVO given when it is destroyed to mitigate its current impact in game, especially in PvP, while keeping its defensive PvE potential against Bosses. 

[b]EVO given on destruction:[/b] Increased from [2] to [3]

[list]
[*] [i][b]The Anvil[/b][/i]
[/list]

The Anvil was able to produce too many Forged Orbs over a too long duration. We limited the generation potential to 3 Orbs over 3 turns. 

[b]Auto-Smithing ability: [/b]

Self-Damage increased from [1] to [2]

[b]New statistics: [/b]

PV increased from [5] to [6]


[h3][b]BUFFS[/b][/h3]


[list]
[*] [i][b]Azog[/b][/i]
[/list]

This mutant had a passive ability with an extremely situational impact. We decided to add it a new Tactics ability, allowing it better possibilities to interact with Mystic decks, while adjusting its statistics towards its defense. 

[b]New statistics: [/b]

ATK reduced from [3-5-7-11-14] to [2-4-5-7-10]

HP increased from [3-5-6-7-10] to [3-5-6-8-12]

[b]New ability:[/b]

Chamanic Strength - Tactics - While you control a Mutant with an Active ability, this mutant has +[2-3-4-5-7] ATK. 

[list]
[*] [i][b]Marship Mallow[/b][/i]
[/list]

This mutant was weaker than planned at the Basic rank, so we slightly improve its attack. 

[b]New statistics: [/b]

ATQ increased from [1-2-4-6-7] to [2-2-4-6-7]

[list]
[*] [i][b]Ghostmonaut[/b][/i]
[/list]

The ability of this mutant used to trigger when one of your buildings was destroyed. Even though it had Evasion, it was usually far more interesting to destroy it before attacking buildings. Its new version deals a little less damage, but now applies when a building on either your or your opponent’s battlefield is destroyed, allowing it to be played in Space archetypes revolving around Cityscape, Deployment and Demolition.

[b]Space Debris ability: [/b]

[i]Before[/i]

Passive - Whenever one of your buildings is destroyed, this mutant deals [2-2-3-4-6] damage to the opposing mutant with the lowest HP. 

[i]After[/i]

Passive - Whenever a Building on either your or your opponent's battlefield is destroyed, this mutant deals [1-1-2-3-5] damage to the opposing mutant with the lowest HP. 

[list]
[*] [i][b]Bushi[/b][/i]
[/list]

As all mutants with Boneyard abilities, its ability didn’t reward enough the risks taken to activate it. We readjusted its statistics and focused its ability towards a better offensive power. 

[b]New statistics: [/b]

ATK increased from [2-2-4-6-9] to [2-3-5-7-9] 

HP reduced from [2-4-6-8-10] to [2-3-5-7-9]

[b]Veterancy ability: [/b]

[i]Before[/i]

Boneyard - While you have at least 10 cards in your Discard, this mutant has +[2-2-3-4-6] ATK and +[2-2-3-4-6] HP.

[i]After[/i]

Boneyard - While you have at least 10 cards in your Discard, this mutant has +[2-3-4-5-7] ATK.

[list]
[*] [i][b]Dead Bot[/b][/i]
[/list]

As all mutants with Boneyard abilities, its ability didn’t reward enough the risks taken to activate it. We decided to increase the Armor bonus given by its ability, granting it a huge potential to attack other mutants. 

[b]Reactive Shielding ability: [/b]

Armor bonus increased from [1-1-2-2-4] à [2-2-3-4-5]

[list]
[*] [i][b]Mirror Reflector[/b][/i]
[/list]

This building was not very popular, due to its complex triggering conditions and a random targeting. We changed its targeting to focus weaker mutants to give it more offensive capabilities. 

[b]Energy Inverter ability:[/b]

[i]Before[/i]

Whenever one of your mutants is healed, deal 1 damage to a random opposing mutant. 

[i]After[/i]

Whenever one of your mutants is healed, deal 1 damage to the opposing mutant with the lowest HP.

[list]
[*] [i][b]Drill Orb[/b][/i]
[/list]

Due to the appearance of the Forged Orb, we improved it to give it an edge over the generated Orb card. 

[b]New statistics: [/b]

HP bonus while equipped to a mutant increased from [0] to [1]


[h3][b]REWORKS[/b][/h3]


[list]
[*] [i][b]Warrior[/b][/i]
[/list]

This starter mutant had a Tactics ability with a harsh activation condition, making it too complex to play efficiently. We changed its ability to have its attack bonus while a mutant is on the opposing battlefield. 

[b]Sanguinary ability: [/b]

[i]Before[/i]

Tactics - While an opposing mutant is damaged, this mutant has +[1-1-2-3-4] ATK.

[i]After[/i]

Tactics - While your opponent controls a mutant, this mutant has +[1-1-2-3-4] ATQ.

[list]
[*] [i][b]Charon[/b][/i]
[/list]

The guardian of the Styx was too slow and unefficient in its previous role. Now as a guardian of Hell, it has a Boneyard ability giving it a massive attack bonus while active. 

[b]Stygian Flows ability:[/b]

[i]Before[/i]

Passive - Whenever a card enters your opponent’s Discard, this mutant has +[1] ATK.

[i]After[/i]

Boneyard - While you have at least 10 cards in your discard, this mutant has +[6] ATK. 

[list]
[*] [i][b]Commander Ender[/b][/i]
[/list]

As all mutants with Boneyard abilities, its ability didn’t reward enough the risks taken to activate it. We reworked this mutant to improve its terrifying side. The mutant is now an Advanced mutant, has its statistics readjusted accordingly, and now also applies an attack penalty to opposing mutants in addition to its autorepair bonus. It now no longer has additional HP depending on allied discards content. 

[b]Mutant Subtype:[/b] Basic → Advanced

[b]Evolution curves: [/b]

EVO necessary to evolve: [2-3-4-5]

EVO given on destruction increases from [1-3-4-6-9] to [2-3-4-6-9]

[b]New statistics: [/b]

ATQ changes to [2-4-6-8-10] 

PV changes to [3-5-6-8-11]

[b]Unstoppable ability: [/b]

[i]Before [/i]

For each allied discard pile that contains at least 10 cards, this mutant has Autorepair [1-1-1-2-3] and  +[0-0-1-2-3] PV.

[i]After[/i]

For each allied discard pile that contains at least 10 cards, this mutant has Autorepair [1-1-2-2-3] and opposing mutants have -[1-1-1-2-3] ATK. 

That's it for this patch,

Hope you'll enjoy it! Have a great day!

Team Mutants Genesis

Victor, your favorite coach and teacher at the Panakeïa Orphanage will be with us again, hello Victor!

[quote=Victor]"Hello everyone! Always a pleasure to be with you."[/quote]

Today we're going to talk about Heroic Cards, the highest rarity in Mutants: Genesis.

[quote=Victor]"These cards are so rare that they can only be played once in your decks!"[/quote]

That's right! When Heroic Cards are Mutants, they must be incubated most of the times! This incubation time is usually ranging from 2 to 4 turns.

[quote=Victor]"But there are also Heroic Cards that aren't Mutants, and I think we'll take a look at those too."[/quote]

Let's start by dwelling on the Heroics you'll get when you manage to beat Victor and all of his different Gene decks during the Campaign before diving in the rest of the collection  available.

Without any preference whatsoever, let's start with Mystic!

[quote=Victor]"Sure..."[/quote]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/2b107f3201dd79dd0a3ecbc317b1034d9b581ebc.png[/img]

[i][b]Geomega[/b][/i] is a card that requires 3 Turns to incubate, that's a long time! So it will have its place in a rather Control deck or one that can deal with the board!

[quote=Victor]"And if you don't know what a Control deck is we invite you to read one of the articles we did, right [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/2138570/announcements/detail/3657532668118790845]here[/url]."[/quote]

[i][b]Geomega[/b][/i] has a devastating active power which makes it a Heroic that works very well on its own or in decks that capitalize on active powers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/527be506c3f7685afd31269e1115d10b14e6eacc.png[/img]

[quote=Victor]"Zeus is the first heroic card in the Space Decks. He specializes in destroying buildings!"[/quote]

And on top of that, it's got some serious stats. Why so serious by the way?

[quote=Victor]"Ahem... Undeads are pretty much serious, look at the [i][b]Forgotten One[/b][/i]!"[/quote]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/8f00e6c3216191199d326d70b8fe14aec6d10c54.png[/img]

This card has [i]Guardian[/i], which coupled to its abilities makes it a very tenacious element of the field. This card is perfect for decks that want a big threat and have the means to temporize its arrival.

Now let's talk about Blades' Heroics!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/573c26f3b31cce4dd75725c91bb80f34fa6e53a2.png[/img]

[quote=Victor]"This is Spartaaaaaaaac! Oops... Sorry."[/quote]

[i][b]Spartac[/b][/i] s a card that fits into Blades Decks, which focus on [i]Orbs[/i]. It can become extremely powerful very quickly, thanks to its ability to tutor an Orb and play it on himself. Once again, however, it will take 3 turns for it to arrive.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/744082db0ed89b44d583092c0e872f51352fad92.png[/img]

[i][b]Goliath[/b][/i] is the Heroic Tech by definition. It will boost itself when [i]Parts[/i] are played on it.

[quote=Victor]"What's more, the addition of Guardian on this card makes it a living wall and justifies its incubation time."[/quote]

Well Victor, I guess I'll let you announce this one....

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/6605b6d46927bb81aafa6a7e03ad4c9ac1e30d59.png[/img]

[quote=Victor]"The [i][b]Solar Lampyrion[/b][/i]! THE Zoo Heroic and my favorite. This pretty beast has no equal when it comes to cleaning up the grounds, a bit like [i][b]Geomega[/b][/i] but... better!"[/quote]


Let's say it's different, [i][b]Solar Lampyrion[/b][/i] has great stats but needs to attack to apply its effect. His passive also allows Mutants to evolve more quickly and can therefore turn the game around very quickly.

Then, of course, there are other heroic Mutants in each gene, which we'll take a look at one after the other.

[list]
    [*]MYSTIC
[/list]

[quote=Victor]"This is your favourite Gene, isn't it?"[/quote]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/e7990be56f91e1ebf733647cb8210c7da72f4daa.png[/img]

That's right! [i][b]Gorthaur[/b][/i] and the [b]Shadow of Kukulkan[/b] are the other two mainly Mystic Heroic Mutants. Both fit into a Burn Deck logic but don't have exactly the same power and Body, you can also play [i][b]Lady Cidohna[/b][/i] who we'll talk more about with the Necros.

[quote=Victor]"Body" is the somewhat barbaric term for a card's set of stats. The higher its stats, the more qualitative it is. A bit like me!"[/quote]

What's important to define when integrating a Heroic into your deck is its rhythm. You need to know whether the number of turns required to incubate it can be easily managed without resorting to Advanced Mutants.

[list]
    [*]SPACE
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/85a5202e76ba8f06f9706d71da726619bf929f59.png[/img]

[i][b]Dreadnought[/b][/i] is the other Heroic mainly Space and playable by this gene.

[quote=Victor]"It will fit easily into Techs and Squad Decks to capitalize on its two abilities."[/quote]

[i][b]Sun-Duke[/b][/i] is another mutant with both genes, but we'll talk more about that in Blades! [i][b]Darwin[/b][/i] can also be integrated into Space Decks, but I'll let Victor explain it better with the focus on Zoo Heroes.

[list]
    [*]NECRO
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/7ed30c10d7a26bab37c78416d7f3cf0afb6bb3a4.png[/img]

[quote=Victor]"[i][b]Charon[/b][/i] and [i][b]Lady Cliodhna[/b][/i] are quite unique! You've got to admit that among the Necros, the Heroics really have style."[/quote]

Charon's mechanic is based on discarding cards, which is very original for the moment, but can make it a formidable card that turns certain games upside down, depending on what's going to be discarded.

[i][b]Lady Cliodhna[/b][/i] is a perfect fit for a deck with active powers, or one that needs to make effective trades thanks to its ability.

We mustn't forget [i][b]Neo-Urban XIII[/b][/i], but we'll come back to it when we talk about Techs!

[list]
    [*]BLADES
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/b8f603a20aad43c99149c76704f6599efdfcc975.png[/img]

[i][b]Spartac[/b][/i] is the true poster child of this gene, but he can be accompanied in decks by [i][b]Sun Duke[/b][/i] for the union between Blades and Space in Squad decks, whose stats make him a formidable foe after just 2 turns! [i][b]Gorthar[/b][/i] can add a little indirect damage and burn effects!

[i][b]Charon[/b][/i] is also a possibility, making Blade Decks rather flexible, with Heroics with 2 Incubation Turns and effects that don't depend on specific mechanics!

[list]
    [*]TECH
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/fc8d127865e1974b8331a24990892f1b4f1fed24.png[/img]

[quote=Victor]"Ah techies, always playing with their [i]Parts[/i]. But it's pretty damn effective!"[/quote]

[i][b]Mecharachnidian[/b][/i] and [i][b]Neo-Urban XIII[/b][/i] join the mainly Techs heroics.

[quote=Victor]"The former has a very zoo feel, who wouldn't want to look like a spider? [i][b]Mecharachnidian[/b][/i] fits in very well with games around [i]Auto-Repair[/i] and is an immediate threat when she arrives on the field!"[/quote]

[i][b]Neo-Urban XIII[/b][/i] is a substantial bodysuit too but above all, a time bomb that forces your opponent to make disadvantageous choices to deal with it.

[i][b]Dreadnought[/b][/i] can also be integrated into Tech Decks to benefit from its [i]Parts[/i] effect.

[list]
    [*]ZOO
[/list]

[quote=Victor]"THE BE(A)STS!"[/quote]

We suspected as much Victor...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/8a6101b78fd493262026240f494cf48fc140a8f3.png[/img]

[quote=Victor]"We're back with [i][b]Mecharachnidian[/b][/i], whom I was telling you about earlier! His skills and stats make him a very good choice whatever the direction of the Deck. [i][b]Darwin[/b][/i] is slower, but his ability to provoke numerous evolutions makes him formidable!""[/quote]

And finally, the [i][b]Shadow of Kukulkan[/b][/i] offers the possibility of Burning opponents with Zoos cards!

[quote=Victor]"And what's more, it's a big snake!!! I love it!!!"[/quote]


As you can see, there are 4 Heroic Mutant options per Gene. Each of them has a big impact when they come into play. To choose, try to maximize the synergies they offer with the rest of your Deck, but also pay attention to the incubation time! Many Heroic cards invite you to build decks around particular gene combinations.

[quote=Victor]"If you have a rather Aggro Deck, favor short incubation times, for example!"[/quote]

And on the contrary, the more Control you are, the more Heroics with a slow incubation you can integrate in youir deck!

Finally, there are two cards that are not Mutants: [i][b]Portal of the Void[/b][/i] and [i][b]Revival[/b][/i]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/d3f12ecc78bb88a080a8ac90ded7d4e34cb1732b.png[/img]

The first is an excellent Removal, which we already mentioned in our article about them. As for [i][b]Revivifying[/b][/i], it's a very practical card that allows you to potentially play several Basic Mutants in a single turn! Use it at the right moment and you're guaranteed an effective board!

Here you are for a roundup of the Heroic Cards! We hope you liked it!

[quote=Victor]"See you later for more articles!"[/quote]

See you soon Psycogs!

Team Mutants: Genesis

notes.title: Mutants: Genesis - Balancing Patch Season 1
notes.content:
Dear Psycogs, 

Welcome to this first Card Balance Patch! Season 1 2023 was dominated by Zoo decks including  [i][b]Beast[/b][/i] as well as Tech Decks.
The objective of this balancing was to reverse the meta and push new deck archetypes forward while lowering the impact of the most present decks.

You'll be introduced to Nerfs and Buffs. Respectively modifications to make a card less or more powerful.

[b]This patch will be online Wednesday 19 2023![/b]

Let's go together through the details:

[h3][b]CARDS NERFS[/b][/h3]

[list]
[*][i][b]Beast[/b][/i]
[/list]
[i][b]Beast[/b][/i] is one of the most powerful and played starter mutant.  We are lowering the damages of its evolving ability in higher ranks to lower its impact in ultra agressive Zoo decks.

[b]Ability Midnight Fang : Damages reduced from [1-1-2-3-4] to [1-1-1-2-3][/b]

[list]
[*] [i][b]Monocerus[/b][/i]
[/list]
[i][b]Monocerus[/b][/i] was initially planned to be played in multiplayer modes. Still, its ability to generate a lot of Parts, even if its just Repair Nanites, make it too powerfull as a Part generator in PvP. We'll be lowering its ability to generate parts in higher ranks and adjust its stats accordingly.

[b]Ability Nanites Production : Number of parts reduced from [1-1-2-3-4] to [1-1-1-1-2][/b]

[b]New Stats:
ATK - [2-3-5-7-10] → [2-3-5-8-10]
HP - [2-3-5-7-10] → [2-3-6-9-11][/b]

[list]
[*] [i][b]Cyber-Croc[/b][/i]
[/list]
Just as [i][b]Monocerus[/b][/i], [i][b]Cyber-Croc[/b][/i]'s ability to generate parts without any cost make it a staple of Tech-Gadget decks. We'll be lowering its ability to generate Parts and raise the number of EVO needed to its evolution. Stats are adjusted accordingly.

[i]Note :[/i] Its stats and the number of EVO given will be adjusted with its new evolution curb.

[b]Ability Mechanisation : Number of parts reduced from [1-1-2-3-4] to [1-1-1-2-3][/b]

[b]Evolution curb : EVO needed to evolve [1-2-3-4] to [2-3-4-5]
[/b]

[b]New Stats:
ATK - [2-3-5-7-10] → [2-3-6-8-11][/b]

[list]
[*] [i][b]Leviathan[/b][/i]
[/list]
Star of OTK Zoo deck before our hotfix of [i][b]Natural Selection[/b][/i] and [i][b]Savage Strike[/b][/i], [i][b]Leviathan[/b][/i] remains a very powerful mutant able to combo with itself. We'll be lowering the damages of its ability to make it harder to evolve it in quick successions in order to destroy all the buildings and damage heavily the psycore.

[b]Ability Tsunami : Damages reduced from [1-2-2-3-4] to [1-1-2-2-3]
[/b]

[list]
[*] [i][b]Cernunnos[/b][/i]
[/list]
Cernunnos' stats were a bit too high. We'll be lowering its attack to put it back in a correct progression curve.

[b]New Stats: ATK lowered from [2-4-6-8-10] to [2-3-5-7-9]

[h3][b]CARDS BUFFS[/b][/h3]

[list]
[*] [i][b]Thor[/b][/i]
[/list]
[i][b]Thor[/b][/i]'s abilities have been reinforced to better work with themslves and make the mutant stronger while rewarding players who discard cards from both genes.

[b]Ability Thunder Shock[/b]

[i]Before[/i]
If you've discarded a Blade mutant, inflicts damages to all other mutants on the target's field.
[i]After[/i]
If you've discarded a Blade mutant, inflicts [1-1-2-2-3] to the target and all other mutants on the field.

[b]Ability Lightning Bolt[/b]

[i]Before[/i]
If you've discarded a Mystic mutant, inflicts Stasis to the target Mutant.
[i]After[/i]
If you've discarded a Mystic mutant, inflicts Stasis [1-1-2-2-3] to all affected Mutants.

[b]Stats adjustment: 
HP : [3-5-6-9-12] → [3-5-7-9-12][/b]

[list]
[*] [i][b]Cursed Mausoleum[/b][/i]
[/list]
The ability Cursed Mausoleum has been modified to have an immediate impact when it arrives on the field.

[i]Before[/i]
At the end of your turn, create a Bones card in your discard.

[i]After[/i]
When it enters play and at the start of the turn, create a Bones card in your discard.

[list]
[*] [i][b]Catacomb Excavation[/b][/i]
[/list]
The number of Bones created has been upped.

[i]Before[/i]
Create 2 Bones in your discard.

[i]After[/i]
Create 3 Bones in your discard.

[list]
[*] [i][b]Howlosaurus[/b][/i]
[/list]
The second Zoo starter suffers from its opposition to [i][b]Beast[/b][/i]. Stats have been balanced to make it more polyvalent.

[b]New Stats:
ATK: [1-1-2-2-3] to [1-2-3-4-6]
HP: [1-3-4-6-9] to [1-2-3-4-6][/b]

[list]
[*] [i][b]The Forgotten[/b][/i]
[/list]
The basic heroic of the Necro gene suffers from a lack of impact when it arrives in game. Giving it the 
[i]Guardian[/i] ability forces the opponent to sacrifice mutants against it, fuelling its ability.

[b]New Keyword: Guardian[/b]

[list]
[*] [i][b]Zeus[/b][/i]
[/list]
The basic heroic of the Space gene gets a new defensive aspect to capitalize on its ability.

[b]New Stats: 
HP: 8 => 7[/b]

[b]Ability added: 
Olympos : Architecture - While you have a building, Zeus has Armor 2[/b]

[list]
[*] [i][b]Lady Cliodhna[/b][/i]
[/list]
The banshee queen gets a new defensive keyword. Her HP stats have been adapted in consequence.

[b]New Stats: 
HP : 7 => 6

New Keyword: Evasion.
[/b]

[list]
[*] [i][b]Darwin[/b][/i]
[/list]
The negative effect of its Rush ability was not rewarding players that were able to summon [i][b]Darwin[/b][/i]. His ability has been modified to entirely remove the negative effect. His stats have been slightly adjusted to account for this change.

[b]Ability Evolution Theory[/b]

[i]Before[/i]
When Darwin enters play, each other Mutants on the field gains 3 EVO and Darwin looses 1ATK and 1HP for each affected mutant.

[i]After[/i]
When Darwin enters play, each other Mutants on the field gains 3 EVO.

[b]Modified Stats:
ATK : 13 => 12
HP : 13 => 12[/b]

[list]
[*] [i][b]Shade of Kukulkàn[/b][/i]
[/list]
Shade of Kukulkàn has a very powerful effect when he arrives in play but his threat level diminishes afterward. A new ability has been added.

[b]New Ability:
Persisting Flames: Passive - At the start of the turn, inflicts Burn 2 to all opposing mutants.[/b]

[list]
[*] [i][b]Dreadnought[/b][/i]
[/list]
The defensive ability of [i][b]Dreadnought[/b][/i] has been reinforced. Its stats have been adapted in consequence.

[b]Modified Stats:
HP : 10 => 8

New Keyword: Armor 2[/b]

[list]
[*] [i][b]Tengu[/b][/i]
[/list]
Like [i][b]Thor[/b][/i], [i][b]Tengu[/b][/i]'s ability has been modified to offer better combos with its 2 other effects.

[quote]NOTE : Tengu will be updated in the next patch as we've encountered some technical issues that prevented it from being released today (19/07).[/quote]

[b]Ability Amnesia[/b]

[i]Before[/i]
If you've discarded a Zoo mutant, this mutant gains X EVO, X ATK and X HP.

[i]After[/i]
If you've discarded a Zoo mutant, this mutant gains X EVO, X ATK and X HP for every target hit.

[list]
[*] [i][b]Soul Pit[/b][/i]
[/list]
The power of [i][b]Soul Pit[/b][/i] has been upped to put it in the same level as cards like [i][b]Missile Turret[/b][/i] or [i][b]Imperishable Blaze[/b][/i]. 

[i]Before[/i]
When a mutant with Last Will you control is destroyed, inflicts 1 damage to the opposing Psycore.

[i]After[/i]
When a mutant with Last Will you control is destroyed, inflicts 2 damages to the opposing Psycore.

[list]
[*] [i][b]Incubator Pod[/b][/i]
[/list]
The resistance of the [i][b]Incubator Pod[/b][/i] has been upped to make it more difficult to destroy mutants incubating in it.

[b]New Stats:
HP: 4 => 5[/b]


[h3][b]CARDS REWORK[/b][/h3]


[b]Ability Ignite[/b]

The Ignite ability was a bit too weak defensively speaking. We are modifying the way it works so it triggers when your Mutants are attacked as well:

Ability modification:

[i]Before[/i]:
Ignite X - Everytime this Mutant attacks another Mutant, it also inflicts Burn X.

[i]After[/i]:
Ignite X - Everytime this Mutant inflicts battle damage, it also inflicts Burn X.

[b]Concerned Cards:[/b]

[list]
[*] [i][b]Demon[/b][/i]
[*] [i][b]Pit Lord[/b][/i]
[*] [i][b]Gorthaur the cruel[/b][/i]
[*] [i][b]Kung Chow[/b][/i]
[*] [i][b]Steam Warlord[/b][/i]
[/list]

[list]
[*] [i][b]Pit Lord[/b][/i]
[/list]

Following changes made to Ignite, the passive ability of Pit Lord became obsolete. He now has a new Aura ability.

[b]Ability Incandescent [/b] - Removed
[b]Ability Inferno[/b] - Modified

[i]Before[/i]
Aura - Double Burn effects on ennemy Mutants (Only at Platinum rank)

[i]After[/i]
Aura - All your Mutants have Ignite [1-1-1-2-3]

[list]
[*] [i][b]Mecharachnidian[/b][/i]
[/list]
[i][b]Mecharachnidian[/b][/i] wasn't working properly. It became a highly played card because its stats where too high because of how its ability worked. 
The card has been reworked to fit its initial design : one of a menace that transforms with time.

[b]New Stats:
ATK: 6, HP: 6, Armor 3[/b]

Ability Shapeshifting: Changes

[i]Before[/i]: 
Passive - At the start of your turn, this mutant has +6 ATQ until the end of the turn. At the start of your opponent's turn, this mutant has Armor 3 until the end of the turn.

[i]After[/i]:
Passive - When this mutant takes damage, it loses all its Armor stacks. While this mutant has no Armor, it has +3 ATK and Autorepair 3.

[list]
[*] [i][b]Gargantua[/b][/i]
[/list]
[i][b]Gargantua[/b][/i]'s abilities have been entirely changed to make it more polyvalent.

[b]Ability Meteor Strike
Base Damages:[1-2-3-4-5][/b]

[b]Ability Direct Impact[/b]

[i]Before[/i]:
If you've discarded a Space mutant, inflicts additionnal damages to the target.

[i]After[/i]:
If you've discarded a Space mutant, deals damage to all ennemy buildings in addition to the target.

[b]Ability Sismic Wave[/b]

[i]Before[/i] :
If you have discarded a Tech mutant, deals damages to all buildings on the target field.

[i]After[/i] :
If you've discarded a Tech mutant, generates [1-1-2-2-3] Parts depending on the number of targets hit.

New Stats:

[b]ATK : [3-5-7-9-12] → [2-4-6-8-10][/b]

[list]
[*] [i][b]Goliath[/b][/i]
[/list]
[i][b]Goliath [/b][/i]'s ability could be frustrating because a lot of Parts cards couldn't see their effects doubled. He got reinforced to become more defensive and decisive. 

[b]New Keyword: Guardian[/b]

[b]Ability Advanced Robotic[/b]

[i]Before[/i]:
Double the effects of the Parts played on him
[i]After[/i]:
Goliath earns +1HP Max et +1 Autorepair each time a Part is played on him.

[list]
[*] [i][b]Neo-Urban XIII[/b][/i]
[/list]
[i][b]Neo-Urban XIII[/b][/i] was suffering from 2 problems: he didn't have enough impact in Necro decks and wasn't impactful enough when he arrived after 4 turns of incubation. His base ability is reinforced and a new ability replace the previous one.

[b]Ability Violent Extraction[/b]

[i]Before[/i]:
Execution: When this mutant destroys another mutant, create 2 Parts in your hand.

[i]After [/i]:
Exécution: When this mutant destroys another mutant, create 3 Parts in your hand.

[b]Ability Artificial Life[/b]

[i]Before[/i]:
Passive - When a Part is played on this mutant, it gains ATK, HP and Autorepair.

[i]After[/i]:
Last Will: When Neo-Urban XIII is destroyed, if it's not your turn, it deals its ATK to the main opposing entity.

[list]
[*] [i][b]Void Turret[/b][/i]
[/list]
The offensive potential of [i][b]Void Turret[/b][/i] was too weak compared to other options. Its ability has been modified.

[i]Before[/i]:
Collapse: When this building is destroyed, inflicts 3 to the mutant that attacked it.

[i]After[/i]:
Collapse: When this building is destroyed, inflicts 3 piercing damage to a random opposing mutant.

[list]
[*] [i][b]Valkyrie[/b][/i]
[/list]
[i][b]Valkyrie[/b][/i] had trouble to find its place in any archetype. A new Tactics ability has been added to help it find a place in an archetype. A new Last Will has been added to ease it's integration in Blade decks while keeping its invocation theme.

[b]New Ability: 
Valhalla's Bond : Tactics - If you have a Warrior on the field, all your blade mutants have +[1-1-2-2-3] ATK [/b]

[b]New Stats:
HP: [1-2-2-3-5] à [0-1-1-2-3][/b]

[list]
[*] [i][b]Solar Lampyrion[/b][/i]
[/list]
[i][b]Solar Lampyrion[/b][/i] was too hard to deal with and plan with. Its ability has been simplified to make it more easy to use.

[b]Ability Solar Eruption[/b]

[i]Before[/i]:
Passive - When this mutant attacks, share all damages inflicted among all opposing entities.

[i]After[/i]:
Passive - When this mutant attacks, deal 3 damages to all opposing entities.

[b]New Stats: 
ATK : 8 → 8
HP : 10 → 10[/b]

[list]
[*] [i][b]Second Chance[/b][/i]
[/list]
Rework of the card to work with the Bones archetype.

[i]Before[/i]:

Discard a Necro mutant: Invoke a Zombie.

[i]After[/i]:
Discard a Necro mutant: Invoke a Silver Rank Ossembly.


Here you go for this patch!

Again, it will be out [b]Wednesday 19th July[/b] and we can't wait to see which decks you'll build!

Have a great day!

Team Genesis

notes.title: Psycog 101 - Drawing
notes.content:
Hello Psycogs! And welcome to this new Psycog 101!

Victor is still with us, the best of coaches!

[quote=Victor]"Hahaha ! Flattery will get you nowhere. But you can keep them coming...!"[/quote]

Drawing is one of the fundamentals of any card game, cards being your actions, it is primordial to have as many as possible.

[quote=Victor]"This is why it's mandatory to include drawing cards in your deck, either under the effects of some Mutants, [i]Support[/i] or [i]Building[/i] cards!"[/quote]

The first introduction we have to drawing cards are [i][b]Genetic Cycling[/b][/i] cards that we obtain fairly early in the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/423b0294e4f54d8f9d6cd24da5b81db8af98c7fe.png[/img]

[i][b]Genetic Cycling[/b][/i] all work the same and ask that you discard a Mutant of the same gene as the card.

[quote=Victor]"This card allow to quickly understand the ressource system of Mutants: Genesis, cards and especially our starter are our ressources!"[/quote]

It is highly encouraged to use your ephemeral starter, that will spawn in your hand each turn, as a ressource when a card requires a discard.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/e3e5726fb509aab4ca22eb52afa17f3d39f6a348.png[/img]

[quote=Victor]"We shouldn't forget [i][b]Bio-Recycling[/b][/i]! One of my favourites!"[/quote]

This card seems bad at first glance: who would like to sacrifice a Mutant and give its EVO to your opponent just to draw? Still it becomes very strong in certain conditions!

The first one is simple, using it on a invoke that is not a Starter or a Fantassin will not give any EVO to the opponent!

[quote=Victor]"The second one asks to play it on your Starter when the board is empty so you don't give any EVO!"[/quote]

This card will easily be played in decks that invoke Mutants on the field.

There is finally a support card specific to Necro users: [i][b]Astralgomancy[/b][/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/28989b3b9d66a9406b03e922ff8f1a16255e3e6e.png[/img]

This one allows to have a strong use of [i][b]Bones[/b][/i] in your deck with a huge draw !

[quote=Victor]"It's not an Ultra for nothing!"[/quote]

Support cards aren't the only one that allow you to draw, there is also [b]Buildings[/b]!

We can then talk about two cards you easily get access to: [i][b]Data Bank[/b][/i] and [i][b]Data Fuse[/b][/i]

The first of those one will draw a lot of cards but is an easy target with 3 HP and 1 EVO!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/f9a0b7bbb6688c719cc1afa58601b81ec62ee6e9.png[/img] 

[quote=Victor]"The second one is a given draw but it's just one card. Still, it allows you to protect your building line with its [i]Guardian[/i] ability."[/quote]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/f5a8c0b517415b5704c5c0f289028d1e62f65f5d.png[/img]

Oh and don't forget...

[quote=Victor]"Oh I really like this one, reminds me of forests!"[/quote]

... the [i][b]World Tree[/b][/i] !

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/b787d01187cdeb52332c2f85c951f3a6af7f0153.png[/img]

This card is a very powerfull tool that allow you to draw each turn and heal your Psycore at the start of your round, it is one of the rare cards that can do this.

[quote=Victor]"Yes but don't forget that with only 4 HP it's pretty fragile, the [i][b]World Tree[/b][/i] also gives 3 EVO when it's destroyed!"[/quote]

It's true. Talking about things that like to be destroyed, what if we talked about the Mutant that allows to draw?

[quote=Victor]"The Mutant?"[/quote]

The Mutant, as there is only one at the moment. It's the Lichlock that once destroyed allows you to draw cards. The more ranks you have the more you draw!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/1501c30e406c275b6faee1224e60df667109dd20.png[/img]

[quote=Victor]"It's one of the cards that really shine with [i][b]Mass Cannon[/b][/i]. It's combos we talked about previously!"[/quote]

Oh yeah that's right Victor! But to end this article, why is drawing so important?

[quote=Victor]"Because of the principle of Card Advantage. It's a slightly advanced concept but one you shouldn't ignore."[/quote]

Card Advantage is a way to measure who has the advantage in the game or not. You say that a Player has Card Advantage when they have more cards and possibilites than their opponent. Drawing is a way to gain Card Advantage.

[quote=Victor]"I made you a drawing:"[/quote]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/911955764ff0c42696a7339783f68a2504267746.png[/img]

Ahem yes... It's very... Explanatory. Even if its a bit caricatural, we can understand that Player A with 2 Mutants on the field and 5 cards in hand has 7 possibilities compared to the 5 of their opponent. [b]We can say that Play A has a Card Advantage of 2.[/b]

This does not win you the game but Player A is in a better spot even if we don't know what Player B has in hand. If they have a lot of cards to draw, Card Advantage can shift!


Here we are at the end of this new Psycog 101! We'll see you for more articles!

[quote=Victor]"Do you think they liked my drawing?"[/quote]

Of course they did, of course. See you latter Psycogs!

Team Mutants Genesis

notes.title: Psycog 101 - Removals
notes.content:
Hello every Psycogs! Glad to see you for a new lesson!

Victor, your favorite teacher also makes his comeback!

[quote=Victor]"How are doing my favorite lasses and lads? Today's theme: Removals. A slightly technical term, maybe a bit barbaric, to designate cards that are made to manage the game board!"[/quote]

Those cards are very important and often take the shape of Support cards. They must be used in most of the decks where they will play a primordial role in order to control the game.

3 of the most important cards in this category are available to all Psycogs almost from the start: : [i][b]Explosion[/b][/i], [i][b]Toxic Leak[/b][/i] and [i][b]Foul Play[/b][/i].

[quote=Victor]"Who doesn't like explosing things? I for sure like it! Explosion is perfect to handle any Basic Mutant that just appeared or to help out finish one that evolved a bit too much!"[/quote]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/99e744a193aea68e7f2900a8aea7277fe537aca3.png[/img]

To inflict 2 damages anywhere is very useful. Its versatility allow [i][b]Explosion[/b][/i] can also be used to destroy buildings! Making it a very important tool. If we wanted to be a bit more technical, more than a Removal,[i][b]Explosion[/b][/i] is what we call a [i]Ping[/i], it can inflicts damages to any entity.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/ed06146f2781a2c8abcdfc32449dd8f705b11cc2.png[/img]

[i][b]Toxic Leak[/b][/i] is definitely what we call a Removal, nothing resists it excepts Heroics.

[quote=Victor]"Be careful to not target your own Mutants or their will only be bones left!"[/quote]

To play it, you'll need to sacrifice 2 cards. Ideally, one of them should be your ephemeral Starter that you get each turns as it is made to serve as a ressource. After that, sacrificing a card dead in hand that does not find any opportunity to be played is a good idea.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/cac70cc058cb36a94b551aa3d51d7f07f6f3e78a.png[/img]

Finally, [i][b]Foul Play[/b][/i] is a main asset and defines actually a lot of the way to play the game!

[quote=Victor]"I think its name is fitting... Gmrpf"[/quote]

[i][b]Foul Play[/b][/i] is very powerful but has very strong conditions in order to be played. If your opponent starts to play a lot of Mutants, it even might be interesting to wait and play it on a target with a lot of EVO. In case your opponent is just playing with 2 Mutants on the field,[i][b]Foul Play[/b][/i] might still be played in order to deal with a very annoying Mutant, even if no EVO is earned.

[quote=Victor]"Since [i][b]Foul Play[/b][/i] is in almost all Decks, you need to anticipate it: play a lot of Mutants at the right moment or play it safe!"[/quote]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/7ba0ecad2601f69c6250ff5c9f6074dc103a8d98.png[/img]

[i][b]Into the Void[/b][/i] is very simple in its use.

[quote=Victor]"You can deal with anything!"[/quote]

It's a black hole. Everything disappear and nothing comes out! It's the perfect tool to handle with the worst threats as long as you are willing to sacrifice the EVO tied to the Mutant. If you were wondering which Heroic card to craft first, it might be this one!

Destroying or inflicting direct damages to Mutants is not the only way to deal with them.

[quote=Victor]"Yes, we shoudn't forget a way to do it that I particularly appreciate it. Cooking them! Do you know that I love BBQs?"[/quote]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/199e24d6bd29ac68e4c203cbc21ed2dc779233d6.png[/img]

[i][b]Incinerate[/b][/i] is a Mythic card that has the ability to affect everything on the board. This is the perfect card to handle multiple Mutants with low HPs during the same turn.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/903aee1983ae1fb9b51a44b4d9002f995f969a15.png[/img]

Mystic decks can also play [i][b]Set Ablaze[/b][/i] that allow to apply [i]Burn[/i] 3 on a Mutant, enough to deal 6 damages in 3 turns! It can also, like [i][b]Incinerate[/b][/i], trigger all abilities that use the [i]Burn [/i]effect.

[quote=Victor]"Don't we forget Cannons? I love Cannons!"[/quote]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/ed68839ab86a23186282159d677b7695f1d04a30.png[/img]

Techs are specialists of this beautifulk tool we called Cannons with [i][b]Scrap Metal Cannon[/b][/i] that allow a very efficient removal, especially in decks that generate a lot of Parts!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/dc76b1704410b25d63656ac45723850db4a4d72c.png[/img]

Still, its [i][b]Mass Cannon[/b][/i], available in all decks, that is particularly versatile. This card allows to play very powerful combos. A concrete exemple is present in the last deck list we shared in our latest article [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/2138570/announcements/detail/3647400837473122137]here[/url].

[quote=Victor]"We can use [i][b]Genshiryoku[/b][/i] who's a Zoo by the way! It generally appears on the field with a lot of stats and can attack and then be sacrificed using [i][b]Mass Cannon[/b][/i] to do a lot of damages."[/quote]

This can allow you to win a game sometimes!

As you can see, Removals are very useful and can find their way in most decks. We highly recommend that you play them!

We hope this article was useful.

See you soon Psycogs!

Team Mutants: Genesis

notes.title: Psycog 101 : Orbs
notes.content:
Hello Psycogs and welcome in this first class of Psycog 101!

We have a very special guest: Victor, who'll be doing his best to help us out in this discovery.

[quote=Victor]"What's up kids? We are going to talk about Orbs. Those small pieces of technology have everything to boost your Mutants in various ways."[/quote]

Orbs are not restricted to Blade decks and can be integrated in every decks! We'll be going to back on this at the end of the article :)

Let's start with a basic: [i][b]Power Orb[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/64076e4cdc65d5729233460a732d909f6a25eb6b.png[/img]

This Orb will give +1 ATK to the equipped Mutant. Simple and efficient but where it really shines is its ability to let you draw once the equipped Mutant is destroyed.

[quote=Victor]"Yep! We call this sort of ability: Cycling. It applies to cards that allow you to draw another card. Technicaly, we then don't loose any ressource or advantage, but this concept is a bit harder and explaining it makes me hungry."[/quote]

In the same caategory of Cycling cards, we can find [i][b]Health Orbl[/b][/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/5e42cbd58aafb140e2c688f0ea9cb14ea78d6adf.png[/img]

[quote=Victor]"This one really helps Mutants to stay on the board, especially useful against my Zoos. Oh and it makes you draw as well."[/quote]

Those two orbs can be very powerful and versatile tools that can fit in any deck. So don't hesitate to open up the Deck Builder and play with it!

It then exist another serie of Orbs that are more niche but allow to answer needs that your Deck does not fill usually or to even strengthen your existing synergies.

[quote=Victor]"And that's what is the most important! Synergies! If you take a crocodile, a bull and an eagle, you have water, earth and air coverage! Well it's the same with Mutants! Kinda."[/quote]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/25a37e0bcdb6511ac1d7445e2d47fcb81ffe3e15.png[/img]

[i][b]Fury Orb[/b][/i] is a very powerful weapon, but it will damage you Mutants when equipped. The idea is to place it on cards wit ha lot of HP like: [i][b]Sir Puggington[/b][/i], [i][b]Lichlock[/b][/i] or [i][b]Urgan[/b][/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/848e6cf47be14145b8d8cd9c5024de9520c91564.png[/img]

[i][b]Invasion Orb[/b][/i] is an Orb that works with a strategy where you let your opponent play buildings or punish it.

[quote=Victor]"It can also serve to gain a lot of HP and ATK on a weak Mutant to make very favorable trades!"[/quote]

Trading is the fact to sacrifice a Mutant against another Mutant. Because of the EVO mechanic, you need the opposing Mutant to earn you more than it costs you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/44ce3d0672403fc6080ea4ffd4c301c94f1a9b69.png[/img]

[i][b]Vampiric Orb[/b][/i] is a very useful tool that allow Mutants, especially Advanced ones, to stay on the board longer. It mainly makes trades harder for your opponents.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/53de48078e3abeece3d31c0685b48e008bb7ab1a.png[/img]

[i][b]Drill Orb[/b][/i] adds the Piercing effect in addition to the ATK bonus.

[quote=Victor]"It's very practical if in your matches you face a lot of Mutants with Armor!"[/quote]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/9a7e32ed6235b7bb95e21b946c5b24f17b176476.png[/img]

Speaking of Armor, [i][b]Defensive Orb[/b][/i] adds to your Mutant just that! Great to use on low HP Mutants.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/4b8acb50d2e94518cdf53bee733ee249bc4a0858.png[/img]

It is part of the same category of Orbs as [i][b]Bulwark Orb[/b][/i] that adds HP but mainly Guardian in order to make a very strong front line.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/a014f5f11ffe370a40418cf2a1a474cd320b7214.png[/img]

[i][b]Repairing Orb[/b][/i] adds Auto-repair, allowing your Mutant to heal each turn.

[quote=Victor]"There is great synergies to use with that! Every effects that trigger when a Mutant is healed will work with this Orb!"[/quote]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/ded505ce3f31158723193dd950a644384a98de35.png[/img]

Finally, it's very important to present [i][b]Blazing Orb[/b][/i] that just as [i][b]Repairing Orb[/b][/i] works very well in addition to effects that trigger when a Mutant is Burned.

[quote=Victor]"We are also forgetting a little something, Orbs are great but there is also cards working with them!"[/quote]

There is obviously Mutants that works very well when you play Orbs on them and you'll mainly find them in Blade Decks.

Regarding cards that have a very good synergy with Orbs, we can name: [i][b]Spoils of War[/b][/i] and [i][b]Remelt Steel[/b][/i] that will allow you to draw Orbs from the discard or your deck.

As you can see, Orbs occupy various supporting roles and shouldn't be underestimated even outside of Blade Decks.

[quote=Victor]"Especially those that cycle! As we often say: the more we draw the more we have cards!"[/quote]

Ahem... Yeah, it is right. And drawing is important.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/53a8df7fbccd430269713e4a5eea9bf5f2ad184e.png[/img]

[u][h3]Progress[/h3][/u]

Throughout the season, you'll progress through different ranks. Each rank (below Master) has 4 Divisions.

All players start at Bronze IV.

You can then progress through Bronze III, then Bronze II, then Bronze I until you reach Silver Division IV, and so on. By winning matches and completing PHs, you move up in division and rank. It's not possible to drop down to the next division, nor to drop down in rank.

Once you've reached the Master rank, you've made it to the top (congratulations!). The ranking system then switches. You no longer earn a PH, but you'll see your rank among all the other Masters.

[*] Champion 3 (rank 3)

[/olist]

At the end of each season, when you next log in, you'll receive rewards equivalent to your current rank (division doesn't count).

[b]Gold [/b]= Booster x5, 1c1 Frame and Season Gold
[b]Silver [/b]= Booster x3, 1c1 Frame and Season Silver
[b]Bronze [/b]= Booster x2, 1c1 Frame and Season Bronze

The maximum rank reached gives access to the associated frame for a limited time throughout the following season.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/a330e4310ae271d0877c6b698cc12151308ac6a2.png[/img]

[i]Seasonal PvP reward frames[/i]

[u][h3]Season change[/h3][/u]

At the end of each season, the current season ends and a new one begins.

Rewards are automatically distributed to players, who will receive them via the reward popup the next time they log in (or when they return to the main screen).

Dear Psycogs, 
The big day has arrived! Mutants: Genesis is now available on Steam. You will find below our first patchnote, related to this early access release. 

Thank you for your support and enjoy our game!

The Mutants: Genesis team

[h1]Early Access Patchnote - May 10th, 2023.[/h1]

[h3][u]Mechanics changes[/u][/h3]
A number of new keywords have been introduced in the game, either to clarify how some abilities work, or because enough cards share a common game mechanic to make it a keyword. 

[i]Unstable[/i]
A mutant with Unstable is stronger than average. However, it has an ability with a negative effect (like damaging your Psycore when played, self-inflicting damage…)
Ex : Robot, Steam Warlord

[i]Dual Core[/i]
A mutant with Dual Core can both attack and use its Action Ability during the same turn. 
Ex : Android

[i]Execution (new version)[/i]
Execution abilities now trigger whenever the mutant destroys another mutant.

[i]Reaper[/i]
Reaper abilities trigger whenever another mutant dies (usually any mutant, but there can be exceptions).
Replaces some previous Execution abilities.
Ex : Cerberus, The Forgotten One

[i]Ossuary[/i]
Ossuary abilities become active while you have at least 10 cards in your discard. 
Ex : Bushi, The Collector

[b]The Equip former keyword disappears, to be replaced by 2 new keywords.[/b]

[i]Equipped[/i]
Equipped abilities are active while the mutant has at least one Orb equipped. 
Replaces some Equip abilities. 
Ex : Barbarian

[i]Unsheathe[/i]
Unsheathe abilities trigger whenever you attach an Orb to the mutant. 
Replaces some Equip abilities. 
Ex : Master Shinzo, El Gringo (new version)

[i]Adapt (new version)[/i]
The former Adapt format changes to facilitate integration of mutants with Adapt abilities in multiple archetypes. 

The new keyword : [i]Adapt[/i] - Mutants with Adapt abilities can gain EVO when specific conditions are met.

[b]Former abilities with the Invasion keywords are modified :[/b]

[i]Invasion (new version)[/i]
Invasion abilities now trigger whenever the mutant damages a building. 
Ex : Shell Shock, Marship Mallow

[i]Demolition[/i]
Demolition abilities trigger whenever the mutant destroys a building.
Replaces some Invasion abilities
Ex : Planet Cleaner (new version)

[i]Cityscape[/i]
Cityscape abilities are linked to the presence of non-Psycore buildings on the board. 
Replaces some Invasion abilities
Ex : Alien, Behemoth (new version)

[i]Aura[/i]
Aura abilities grant bonuses or abilities to multiple mutants. 
Numerous mutants with Squad now have their Passive abilities become Auras.  

[i]Status Condition[/i]
The bold gameplay term is added to encompass Burning, Stasis, ATK/HP decreases, and numerous other effects in the future. 

[i]Cleanse[/i]

The gameplay term bold is added, and means “Remove all status conditions”. 

[u][h3]New cards[/h3][/u]
New cards added to the game. 

[i]Building Cards[/i]

[b]Planning Table[/b]
5 HP 
1 EVO
Passive - All your mutants with an active Tactics have +1ATK and +1HP. 

This card reinforces the Blades archetype around the cards with Tactics, which did not have a dedicated building.

[b]Missile Turret[/b]
4 HP
1 EVO
Passive - At the end of your turn, this building deals 2 damage to the Primary Objective.

An aggressive card to put constant pressure on the opponent. Reminder: the Primary Objective is the Psycore or Boss, depending on the game mode.

[b]Engineering Lab[/b]
5 HV
1 EVO
Passive - Whevener one of your mutants is healed by Autorepair, it obtains +1ATK.

This card brings a dedicated building around the cards with Autorepair.

[i]Support cards[/i]

[b]Battle Plan[/b]
For each mutant with an active Tactics on your board, draw a card.  

This card reinforces the Blades archetype around the cards with Tactics, which did not have a dedicated support card.

[b]Strength in Numbers[/b]
Each mutant you control obtains +1ATK this turn. Each Summoned mutant obtains an additional +1ATK. 

We were missing cards to carry a mass attack, so we chose to make it a version that particularly strengthens decks based on filling the board with Summons.

[b]Reconstruction[/b]
Discard a Building: Add a Building from your deck to your hand.  

A very efficient card that allows recycling a building during the game (such as an additional incubator). It also reinforces the theme of Buildings in the Space gene.

[b]Savage Strike[/b]
Discard a card: Target a Zoo mutant you control which deals its ATK as damage to a random opposing entity. 

An aggressive card for Zoo mutants, also usable in PvE against a boss. It remains playable in all decks, if you have mutants with the Zoo gene on the battlefield.

[b]Basic Troopers[/b]
Discard a Space mutant: Summon 2 Basic Troopers with Squad. 

A card that completes the Support card cycle with a discard cost of a certain gene, as well as fixing one of the problems identified around the Squad deck.

[h3][u]Modified/Replaced cards[/u][/h3]
Completely modified cards (major effect/concept change)

[i]Mutant Cards[/i]
A large number of mutants without abilities or with only basic keywords have been modified to better fit with the different archetypes of the game.

[b]Starters[/b]
 
Robot - Tech
ATK 2/3/4/5/7
HP 2/3/4/5/7

Autorepair 1/1/2/2/4
Unstable - When this mutant enters play, your Psycore takes 2 damage. 
The old Robot design did not allow us to have a sufficiently interesting card. Creating an ability with the new keyword Unstable allows us to have a starter with higher base stats, but with a drawback.

[b]Warrior[/b] - Blades
ATK 1/2/3/4/6
HP  1/2/3/4/6

Tactics - While an opposing mutant is damaged, this mutant has +1/1/2/3/4 ATK.
The previous design of the Warrior wasn’t convincing enough for us with its actual form, we wanted to push more of the Tactics archetype through this starter.

[b]Basic[/b]
 
Halbeard - Tech/Mystic
ATK 1/3/5/7/9
HP 2/3/5/7/10

Armor 1/1/1/1/2
Guardian
Unstable - When this mutant attacks, it gets -2 ATK after the fight until the end of your opponent’s turn.

This mutant was lacking impact in his previous version. We gave it a place as a Basic Guardian in Tech and Mystic, while giving it the Unstable trait to have a more defensive mutant.

[b]Ghostmonaut[/b] - Necro/Space
ATK 2/4/6/8/11
HP 2/3/5/7/11

Evasion
Passive - When one of your Buildings is destroyed, inflicts 2/2/3/4/6 damages to the mutant with the least HP.

This mutant was lacking impact. Now it has a spot in decks with buildings that selfdestroy to trigger abilities.

[b]Wampara[/b] - Space/Zoo
ATK 1/2/4/6/9
HP 3/5/7/9/13

Squad
Passive - At the start of the turn, give 1 EVO randomly to one of your mutants with Squad.
This card reinforces Squad with the Zoo evolution thematic.

[b]Micky Krueger[/b] - Necro/Blades
ATK 2/4/6/8/10
HP 2/3/4/6/8

Piercing
Reaper - When an opponent mutant is destroyed, inflicts 1/1/2/2/3 damages to the opponent’s Psycore.

This mutant now applies important pressure on the opponent with small passive damage, preventing their ability to do reckless trades with his own mutants.

[b]Arachno[/b] - Zoo/Tech
ATK 1/2/3/4/6
HP 1/2/3/4/6

Armor 1/1/2/2/3
Dual Core
Action, discard a Tech, Zoo or a Part card: the targeted mutant has -1/2/2/3/5 ATK this turn.

Arachno becomes less passive but also more easy to deal with for your opponent.

[b]Steam Warlord[/b] - Tech/Mystic
ATK 1/2/4/5/7
HP 3/4/6/7/10

Armor 1/2/2/3/3
Ignite 1/2/2/3/5
Unstable - When this mutant attacks, it inflicts Burning 1/2/2/3/3 to itself.

A complete rework of this Mutant’s design that will need to be played alongside cards dedicated to Purge to prevent it from damaging itself too easily.

[b]Kung Chow[/b] - Mystic/Zoo
ATK 1/3/4/6/8
HP 2/4/5/7/10

Ignite 1/1/2/2/3
Passive - Whenever an opposing mutant becomes Burning, this mutants gains 1/1/2/2/0 EVO. (Platinum: Whenever an opposing mutant becomes Burning, you mutants gain 1 EVO)
Adaptation

Kung Chow get stronger with the Adaptation ability and an interaction with Burning mutants. Yes its ability works when the Burning Stacks come from a Support card.

[b]Men'ki Guard[/b] - Blades/Zoo
ATK 1/2/3/5/8
HP 2/4/5/7/10

Guardian
Tactics - While you have another mutant without Guardian, this mutant has +1/2/3/4/5 ATK and Piercing.

We decided to reinforce this mutant’s theme by giving it a Tactics ability associated to it’s Guardian’s role. It gets stronger when it has a mutant to protect.

[b]El Gringo[/b] - Blades
ATK 2/3/4/5/7
HP 2/3/4/5/7

Unsheathe - Whenever this mutant is equipped with an Orb, it deals 1/1/2/2/4 damage to the opposing mutant with the least HP.

El Gringo was too powerful and too redundant with the Barbarian starter. We thus decided to modify its ability to give it Unsheathe fitting more with its visual style.

[b]Captain Patriot[/b] - Space/Tech
ATK 1/3/4/6/9
HP 2/3/5/7/10

Guardian
Space
Passive - For every other mutant with Squad on your board, this mutant gains Autorepair 1/1/2/2/3. 

The fundamental mechanic of Captain Patriot still revolves around being a Guardian with Squad and Autorepair but now we tie it to the Squad ability making it more fitting in decks featuring multiple Squad mutants.

[i]Advanced[/i]

[b]Cernunnos[/b] - Zoo
ATK 2/4/6/8/10
HP 3/5/7/10/13

Guardian
Piercing
Passive - When this mutant defends, it deals 1/2/3/4/6 damage to a random opposing mutant.

The previous ability of Cernunnos was too close to how Tactics work and was too close to Sir Puggington’s ability, this is why we decided to modify it to play more on the random aspect of the Zoo.

[b]Undead Dragon[/b] - Necro/Zoo
ATK 3/5/7/10/12
HP 2/4/6/8/10

Last Will - When this mutant dies, it inflicts -1/2/3/4/5 ATK to all the mutants.  
Undead Dragon had no ability. It now has a powerful but dangerous Last Will effect.

[b]Behemoth[/b] - Space/Blades
ATK 3/4/5/7/9
HP 3/5/7/10/12

Cityscape - For every Building on your board, this mutant has +1/1/2/2/3 ATK and +0/1/1/2/3 HP.
Behemoth was only a mutant without any ability. Now it works well in a deck with a lot of buildings along with the Alien starter.

[b]Dezinger[/b] - Tech/Blades
ATK 2/3/5/6/9
HP 4/5/7/9/13

Autorepair 1/1/2/2/4
Equipped- While this mutant is equipped, it has Guardian and +0/2/2/3/4 HP. 
Dezinger only had stats, it now fits with the Autorepair and Orbs archetypes from those two genes.

[b]Nordic Knightmare[/b] - Blades
ATK 2/4/5/7/9
HP 2/4/6/8/11

Armor 1
Piercing
Tactics - While an opposing mutant has Armor, this mutant has +2/2/3/4/6 ATK.

Nordic Knightmare simply had Armor and Piercing. We are giving it back a place in the Tactics archetype while limiting its Armor. 

[b]Amarok[/b] - Mystic/Blades
ATK 3/4/5/6/9
HP 3/4/6/8/12

Piercing
Tactics - While you don’t have any other mutant, this mutant has +1/2/3/4/5 ATK and+1/2/3/4/5 HP. 
Amarok is now a lone wolf. It must be alone to trigger its Tactics but the boost he gets is very important

[b]Planet Cleaner[/b] -Space/Tech
ATK 3/5/7/10/13
HP 2/4/6/8/10

Piercing
Demolition - When this mutant destroys a building, add 2/2/3/3/5 random Parts to your hand.

Before this mutant didn’t have any stats, it now has a Parts generation ability and its high stats allow it to destroy buildings easily.

[b]Raptoid[/b] - Zoo/Tech
ATK 3/5/6/8/11
HP 2/3/4/6/8

Autorepair 1/1/2/2/3
Passive - Whenever this mutant is targeted by a Parts card, it gains 1 EVO. (Platinum: Whenever one of your mutants is targeted by a Parts card, it gains 1 EVO).

Before, this mutant only had Autorepair. We chose to give it an Adaptation ability tied to Parts, giving it more flexibility in the possible archetypes it can be played in.

[b]R0B-H4N Sentinel[/b] - Tech
ATK 3/6/8/11/13
HP 3/5/6/9/11

Autorepair 1/1/2/2/3
Passive - At the start of the Autorepair phase, if this mutant is undamaged, it gains +1/1/2/2/3 HP. 

This mutant only had the Armor and Autorepair keywords. It no longer has Armor but can increase its maximum HP as long as it’s kept at full health.

[b]Horus[/b] - Mystic/Zoo
ATK 1/2/3/4/6
HP 4/6/7/9/12

Action : Inflicts Burning1/1/2/3/4 to each opposing mutant. 

We decided to modify Horus' ability. Instead of inflicting Burning through Ignite and a Passive at the end of the turn, we decided to give it the ability to do so through an Action Ability. It reinforces its Mystic theme and allows more control to the player.

[i]Building Cards[/i]

[b]Junkyard Crane[/b]
5 HP
2 EVO

Passive - Whenever one of your Tech mutants is destroyed, create a random Parts card in your hand.

The old version of this card had a too complicated trigger (to have a Part in hand at the start of the turn). We decided to keep the idea to get Parts back but associated with the thematic of mutant destruction.

[b]Recycling Tower[/b]
5 HP
2 EVO

Passive - Whenever an Ephemeral card is erased from your hand, heal 1 from your Psycore.

The old version of Recycling Tower often had the same use as the Repair Nanite Parts card. We decided to remove the Part Card Reinforced Structure allowing the Psycore to be healed while adding its effect to this new version of the Recycling Tower.

[b]World-Tree[/b]
5 HP
2 EVO

Passive - At the beginning of your turn, heal 1 to your Psycore and draw a card. 
We felt that the card was largely lacking in power. So we decided to replace its ability to self-maintain with a draw effect. 

[i]Support Cards[/i]

[i]Orbs[/i]

[b]Repair Orb[/b]
The equipped mutant has +1 HP and Autorepair 2.

This highly defensive orb replaces the old version of the Repair Orb. The power of the card has been greatly increased.

[b]Fury Orb[/b]
The equipped mutant has +3 ATK and you immediately deal 2 damage to it. 
This risky offensive orb replaces the old version of the Fury Orb. The old version was an obsolete design. 

[b]Invasion Orb[/b]
The equipped mutant has +1 ATK and +1 HP for each non-Psycore building on your opponent's battlefield.
This orb is consistent with the new version of the Alien. The old version was an obsolete design. 

[b]Vampiric Orb (replaces Sacrifice orb)[/b]
When the equipped mutant damages another mutant, it heals 2 from itself.

This orb replaces the Sacrificial Orb. The former version was a mash-up of test-mechanics moved to other cards during development (Protector Orb and Power Orb).

[b]Blazing Orb (replaces Ignite)[/b]
Whenever the mutant equipped with this orb deals damage to another mutant, il also inflicts Burning 1. 

This orb replaces the Ignite Orb. Instead of limiting the orb to triggering on attacks, it works on all damage dealt (including with abilities).

[i]Gadgets[/i]

[b]Nano-bomb[/b]
Deals 1 damage to any target. 

This Gadget card replaces the Gadget - Reinforced Structure card. The previous one didn't work as well as expected, and in order not to change the number of gadgets available, we have chosen to introduce a gadget capable of inflicting direct damage. The damage is limited, however, so as not to make it an overpowered card. 

[i]Other Support cards[/i]

[b]Psycore Overload[/b]
Your Psycore takes 3 damage. Summon a Basic copy of your Starter mutant.
The card was too powerful in its previous version. So we made the choice to change from a card dedicated to the draw to a card allowing to play more mutants.

[b]Second Chance[/b]
Discard a Necro Mutant. Summon a Zombie. 

The previous version allowing to recover a mutant from the discard pile did not work as expected. So we chose to reinforce the swarming aspect of the Necro. 

[b]Remelt Steel[/b]
Add an Orb card fro your discard pile to your hand. 
We have removed the cost of discarding the card, to make it more interesting. 

[b]Spoils of War[/b]
Discard a Blades Mutant. Add an orb deck from your deck to your hand. 

We removed the randomness, by adding a discard cost. This makes the card more reliable in a deck with many different orb cards.

[u][h3]Rebalanced Cards[/h3][/u]
Cards with more minor changes, often only numerical. 

[i]Mutant Cards[/i]

[b]Honey Bunny[/b] -Basic - Blades/Zoo
ATK 2/3/5/6/9
HP 1/2/4/5/8

Evasion
Tactics - while you have another mutant without Evasion, this mutant has +1/2/3/4/5 ATK
Honey Bunny is now more fragile (while still taking advantage of her Evasion).

[b]The Devourer[/b] - Advanced - Necro/Space
ATK 3/5/7/10/13
HP 3/5/7/10/13

Passive - Once per turn, when a Bones would be added to your discard pile, instead it is erased and this mutant gains +1/1/1/1/2 ATK and +1/1/1/1/2 HP until the end of turn. 
This mutant took advantage far too easily of effects that put several bones in the discard pile, even at the lowest ranks.

[b]Retribution[/b] - Basic - Mystic
ATK 1/2/3/4/5
HP 2/3/5/7/9

Action: Heals 2/3/4/5/8 to target allied mutant and Cleanse all the Status Conditions of the target. 
This mutant was too passive, so we decided to increase its ATK at the expense of its HP. We've also increased its active ability, both in magnitude and by adding the Cleanse effect to all ranks (instead of keeping it only on high ranks).

[b]Cyber-Agent[/b] - Advanced - Blades/Tech
ATK 2/3/4/6/9
HP 2/4/6/8/11

Autorepair 1/1/1/1/2
Tactics - While this mutant is undamaged, this mutant has +2/3/4/5/6 ATK. 
The mutant has been adjusted to give more value to its Tactics, while giving it Autorepair from the Basic rank. 

[i]Support Cards[/i]

[b]Darwinism[/b]
Target Mutant gains 2 EVO. 

The card gives 2 EVO instead of 3, because it was too powerful compared to the power level we wanted for this card.

[b]Small Medpack[/b]
Heals 1 damage from target damaged allied mutant, then draw 1 card. 

The card was used more for its draw effect than for its healing effect. In order to rebalance this, it now requires a wounded mutant to be healed in order to work, and can no longer be played on an intact mutant.

notes.title: Early access feature #1 : the art of crafting
notes.content:
Among the new features available at the early access launch of Mutants: Genesis, today we're having a close up on the deckbuilding menu, specifically the [b]crafting[/b] tool, the must-have for tweaking your decks and gaining power. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/df41c304fa1b42515c359768a93df5069f921e6c.png[/img]

[u][h3]Currency[/h3][/u]
In Mutants: Genesis, it is possible for players to create specific cards from a dedicated currency called [b]Mutagens[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/0d7ed6c6557f3f1608f4bf440f569fed1f1b5053.png[/img] Mutagens logo

This currency is obtained by recycling extra copies of cards obtained through capsules. The player can see how many Mutagens they currently have at the top of the screen.

[u][h3]Recycling[/h3][/u]
When a player opens a capsule, if they get a card that they already have the maximum number of copies of (1 for heroic cards, 3 for all others), then the card is automatically recycled.

In exchange, the player gets a fixed number of Mutagens, depending on the rarity of the card.

[u][h3]Unowned cards[/h3][/u]
From the deckbuilding menu, players can use their Mutagens to create cards of their choice.

The Crafting tool is integrated into the deckbuilding menu: now players can access the unowned cards in their collection. 

These cards will appear when the [i]Unowned[/i] option at the top of the screen is activated. Unowned cards will appear in the collection in a grayed out format. An unowned card can be found in a decklist, if it comes from a deck import. The boxes are also grayed out.

⚠️ [b]If a player does not have enough copies of a card in a list, the owned and unowned copies are split into two boxes: one solid, one grayed out, each with its own copy counter.

When a player interacts with an unowned card (left-click to put it in the deck from the collection, or right-click from anywhere to open the detailed info), the detailed info pops up directly in craft mode.[/b]

[b]Campaign cards are not craftable. ⚠️
[/b]
[u][h3]Copy dots[/h3][/u]
The possession indicator under the cards has been changed.

From now on, there should always be a dot for each maximum possible copy of a card. Heroic cards will always have 1 dot, all others will have 3 dots. These dots have three states: [b]not owned, owned and not present in the deck, and owned in the deck. [/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/0e8194f6e9ffea562bb6d3795f7f88b75c217c2e.png[/img] Unowned
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/0a71d853e72e4483e0ec0c0497e3781425e0ba1f.png[/img] Owned but not in the deck
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/732cd6f4972d78fd2d94ecd3187bebd6acb3bf29.png[/img] Owned in the deck

[h2]Craft Mode[/h2]

In the deckbuilding screen only, the detailed info popup of a card is enhanced.
When a player tries to put a copy of an unowned card into their deck, instead of nothing happening, the game will open the detailed info popup of the card in question, directly opened in Craft mode.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/77891cca87f73f7f3005f6cd038d19e5e0bc470e.png[/img]

In this mode, the player will be able to create a new copy of the card in exchange for his Mutagens.

Here is the information about this special mode in the popup:

[list]
[*] A reminder of the mutagens owned
[*] A reminder of the owned card copies
[*] An information button: when clicked, a popup containing text appears indicating how the crafting system works.

[*] The Craft button: with an upper part depending on the rarity (See below: Special cases: Ultra and Heroic Craft) and several possible situations: 
[*] the player has enough Mutagens
[*] the player does not have enough Mutagens
[*] the player now has the maximum number of copies
[*] the card is not craftable

[*] The mode switching button: by clicking on this button, the player goes back to detailed information mode. He can switch back to craft mode via the same button, also located in detailed information mode[/list].

[u][h3]Special Cases: Ultra and Heroic Cards[/h3][/u]
There is an additional limitation regarding Ultra and Heroic cards crafting.
These cards, in addition to requiring Mutagens, require a special item called the [b]Ultra/Heroic Energy Core.

Players can have a maximum of 3 Ultra Energy Cores and 1 Heroic Energy Core.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/b1f49d53c5f854ff031aa8c3c9525e01393a76ae.png[/img] Ultra
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/8dbcba7001bc4849176aa51f6794ba322e9a3e83.png[/img] Heroic

If a player does not have a Core when attempting to craft Ultra or Heroic, the button is locked. Players will be able to obtain Energy Cores through weekly quests, the Battle Pass, or as event rewards.

[h3]Capsule Information[/h3]
If a player needs to obtain a Core via any means and already has the maximum number, a popup will offer to turn their Core into Mutagens.

[u][h3]Deck Invalidity[/h3][/u]
With the appearance of the crafting system, and the possibility of importing a deck without having all the cards, decks must now have a status of [b]validity or invalidity[/b].

It is possible to have invalid decks in your deck collection, but it is not possible to select them to play with as long as their status is invalid.

An Invalid deck is surrounded by a red effect. A popup window indicates "This deck is invalid, because it is not complete, or contains unowned or temporarily disabled cards".

A deck is invalid if it meets one of these conditions: 

[list]
[*] The deck does not contain 40 cards
[*] The deck contains at least one unowned card
[*] The deck contains at least one deactivated card
[/list]

It is still possible to save an invalid deck. A confirmation popup should ask the player if he/she is sure he/she wants to save this deck despite its status.

In the deck selection screens before deckbuilding, invalid decks appear with the same effect and invalidity icon:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/2570dce0e5828eff13b7f14336dd2ee651f831d6.png[/img]

In the deck selection screen before a fight, the deck is additionally grayed out and not interactive: 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/b5eb2e9be58d35d71b6440ac5a0edc2671f4295c.png[/img]

And that's it! You know everything about the crafting tool. As a reminder, it will be available at the early access launch of Mutants: Genesis! Don't hesitate to give us your feedback in comments, we are very curious to have your opinion on this feature. Join us also on [url=https://discord.com/invite/U4We5hJbXn][b]Discord[/b][/url] to exchange between players, share your decklists and debate about the title of best mutant! 

See you soon on Mutants: Genesis 💪

notes.title: What is Mutants: Genesis?
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

With our game announcement, it is clear we wanted ot give you a bit of details on what is the game and how it is played, so here we go!

[h3][b]So what is Mutants: Genesis?[/b][/h3]

Mutants: Genesis is a free-to-play online card game that makes players take the role of Psycogs, powerful humans with the ability to control mutants.

In Mutants: Genesis your objective will be to prevail on the battlefield by destroying your opponent’s Psycore while defending your own in PvP or defeating the various enemies that will challenge you in PvE.

To do that, you will use a deck of 40 cards that will use a combination of different abilities to ensure your dominance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/fdc6d340323d289fad69322bd0e1fed65edf43fc.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]Mutants: Genesis and its cards[/b][/h3]

Mutants: Genesis is a turn by turn card game. You and your opponent will each take turns to play cards in the best way possible to take the advantage.

First, you’ll have to build a deck by choosing a Gene that will define your Psycore, this will also limit which cards you can put in your deck and your Starting Card. The Starting Card is a basic Mutant that will be available to you each turn.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/c16eae135318f9d0df9b9d6bc365ed550c0f15e3.jpg[/img]

Cards come in different types. You have your Mutants, which are your main tools and can be divided in 3 categories : basic, advanced and heroic. 
[list]
[*] You can play up to 1 basic card each turn directly on the battlefield.
[*] Advanced are generally stronger and will require that you incubate them first for 1 to 2 turns.
[*] Heroics have a huge impact on the game but need more time to incubate.
[/list]
You can have up to 5 Mutants on the field.

Incubation is one of the key differences with other card games. Mutants: Genesis does not have ressources like : mana, lands, etc. Instead, you will need to incubate some Mutants cards by putting them in your Psycore or buildings that allow you to do that. They will then stay there for a set number of turns indicated on the card.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/ef86b590645b9e7d975763ae8989ad848e7b31c7.jpg[/img]

Other cards you can find are: support and buildings. 
[list]
[*] Support cards will trigger an effect when played and then be discarded.
[*] Buildings will take one of the 3 slots available on your board and provide different bonuses or abilities while they are in play : some may allow you to incubate more, draw or trigger specific abilities when you do something in particular.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/ec2ab9e7290b4602077487391580be44e3041d55.jpg[/img]

[i][b]Now here is a quick look about what informations you can find on the Mutant Cards[/b][/i]:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/4c417055cab704fa75073d8fc1418d9eb083563e.png[/img]

Once you have made your deck using those 3 types of cards you are ready to face the challenges of Mutants: Genesis!

[h3][b]How is Mutants: Genesis played?[/b][/h3]

Each player starts with a hand of card, the first player will have 5 and the second 6. You can mulligan, meaning putting back in the deck any number of cards you deem unnecessary in your opening hand and then drawing new ones.

Once this is done, it is your turn: it is now time to try to destroy the opponent’s Psycore!

To do that, you can play:
[list]
[*] Up to one basic mutant and incubate as many mutants as you can - your psycore can incubate up to one mutant if none is currently being incubated. 
[*] As many buildings as you have available slots - up to 3.
[*] As many support cards as you want. 
[/list]
But keep in mind the principle of card advantage! Card advantage is totalling the amount of cards on the board and in your hand, the higher the better : it means you have possibilities of play.

Each turn starts, you’ll draw a card and get your Starting Basic Mutant. Your Mutants can attack directly when they are summoned (Except during the first round of the game!). They can target any mutants or building on the board, except when some abilities like Guardian come into play.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42982631/e079a020e21ff6cb84925c6107b4b6f8cb0a9676.jpg[/img]

All there is left to do is to win the game!

You now know how to play Mutants: Genesis. Don’t worry, when you will get your hands on the game you’ll have the opportunity to go through a Tutorial to learn some more tips and tricks.

Have a great day Students!
